```{r}
#| include: false
## library to inspect objects
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(rlang)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(ggtext)
```

[Q. Difference between `geom_path()` and `geom_line()`]{.question} `geom_path` connects in the order the points appear.
Both recognize `linetype`

[Q. Difference between `geom_rect()` and `geom_tile()`?]{.question} `geom_rect()` has `xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax` whereas `geom_tile()` 
measures coordinates from the center of the rectangle. It has `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`. `geom_raster()` is a [fast special case]{.warning} of `geom_tile()`

(@) `geom_area()` is a good way to color area below the plot.


```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  x = c(3 ,1, 5),
  y = c(2,-4,6),
  label = c("a", "b", "c")
)

df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y, label = label)) +
  geom_area(color = "gray", alpha = 0.7)

```

[Q. How to group based on more than one column?]{.question} Use `aes(group = interaction(school_id, student_id))` 

[Q. How to interpolate more values of y based on interpolated values of x?]{.question}

```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 11:13, color = c(1,3,5))

xgrid <- with(df , seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 10))
xgrid

approx(df$x, df$y, xout = xgrid)
```

(@) [Default `group` asthetics]{.key} `fill` or `color` aesthetic using a [discrete]{.warning} variable makes the variable a `group`
aesthetic as well. So applying `aes(fill = discrete_val)` makes groups the data based on `discrete_val`. This is NOT true when
using a continuous variable for the `fill` asthetic. 


```{r}
# drv is character therefore treated equivalently to factor.
# Here, drv is also a group asthetic. So, for the finest grain grouping the values of fill aesthetic is the same. 
# Hence, they have the same color.
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar()

# Here, the latest grouping is `class`. For each group in class, there are multiple fill colors, so ggplot ignores individual
# color mappings altogether and gives a default gray color to all.
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(class, fill = hwy )) + 
  geom_bar()

# Need to explicitly mention group aesthetic for continuous fill aesthetics.
mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(class, fill = hwy, group = hwy)) +
  geom_bar()

```

(@) Different methods to display **uncertainty**.


```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(18, 11, 16), se = c(1.2, 0.5, 1.0))
cb <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_crossbar()
lr <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_linerange() + geom_point()
sm <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_smooth(stat = "identity")
rb <- df |> ggplot(aes(x, y, ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se)) + geom_ribbon()

cb + lr + sm + rb

```

(@) `bind_2d()` to show distribution . Use `fill = after_stat(density)` 
to use density instead of count.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(2000), y =  rnorm(2000))

df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_bin2d(aes(fill = after_stat(density)))
```

[Q. How to use some other summary function instead of the default count in `geom_bar`?]{.question}

```{r}
diamonds |>
  ggplot(aes(color, price)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "summary_bin", fun = mean)
```

(@) Use `quote()` to include formulas in axis titles


```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.01))
df |>
  ggplot(aes(x)) +
  geom_function(aes(colour = "first"), fun = \(x) x^3) +
  ylab(label = quote(f(x) == x^3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("first" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

(@) Use the `ggtext::element_markdown()` type for the text themes to include bold or italic type.


```{r}
data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 1:3, family = c("sans", "serif", "mono"), fontface = c("plain", "bold", "italic")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x,y)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = family, family = family, fontface = fontface)) +
  xlab(label = "Axis title with *italic* and **bold**") +
  theme(axis.title.x = ggtext::element_markdown())
```
